name: Tali Sree Mahadeva Kshetram (Tali Temple)
tagline: Zamorin’s ancient Shiva shrine — seat of Revathi Pattathanam and living temple traditions.
summary: Historic Tali Mahadeva Temple in central Kozhikode is the Zamorin’s ancient Shiva shrine and the site of the long‑running Revathi Pattathanam scholarly assembly and related temple traditions.
description: Tali Sree Mahadeva Kshetram is an ancient Kerala‑style Shiva temple in the heart of Kozhikode (Palayam). The complex combines laterite, wood carving and mural work and remains a prominent civic and religious landmark.

The temple matters as both a historic royal shrine of the Zamorins and a living centre of learning: for centuries it hosts Revathi Pattathanam, a seven‑day assembly of Sanskrit scholars and philosophers under traditional patronage.

Local tradition and historic accounts link the temple to astrological consultations and ritual inquiry (deva‑prasnam) used by temple committees in Kerala; these practices form part of the temple’s long ritual profile alongside puja and festivals.

Visitors get close views of Kerala temple architecture, small subsidiary shrines, and city life around the Palayam‑tank area; if you time a visit for Revathi Pattathanam (Thulam / Oct–Nov) you see the temple as a functioning scholarly and cultural stage.
highlights: 14th‑century heart of Kozhikode and historic Zamorin shrine.
Revathi Pattathanam — annual seven‑day scholarly assembly (Thulam, Revathi star).
Kerala temple architecture: multi‑tiered tiled roofs, chariot‑shaped sanctum and mural/brass work.
Living ritual traditions (temple committees, periodic astrological inquiries as part of temple practice).

sections.heading: Background
body: Tali Mahadeva Temple sits in Palayam, Kozhikode, and is one of the city’s oldest and most important temples. The present structure and the temple’s prominence date to the medieval period when the Zamorin’s patronage made it a royal shrine.

Historically the site is closely associated with the Zamorin (Samoothiri) dynasty; local and tourism accounts place the temple’s high point in the later medieval era and link it with the rise of Kozhikode as a trade and cultural centre.

sections.heading: Scholarly assemblies and temple‑prasna traditions
body: The temple is best known for Revathi Pattathanam, a traditional seven‑day assembly of Sanskrit scholars and philosophers held from the Revathi asterism in the Malayalam month of Thulam (roughly mid‑October to mid‑November). The Pattathanam historically awarded the title 'Bhatta' and monetary gifts (Bhatta danam) to successful scholars.

Kerala temple culture also preserves deva‑prasnam (ritual astrological inquiry) and related remedial rites; scholarship on Kerala temple astrology describes how temple committees commission such assessments to identify ritual faults and prescribe liturgical remedies. Local tradition connects astrology and ritual inquiry with the temple’s history of dispute, atonement and public patronage.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Walk the temple compound to study the multi‑tiered tiled roofs, the chariot‑shaped sanctum (sreekovil), wooden carvings and brass details. Look for smaller shrines to Ganapati, Bhagavati and other deities that form the temple complex.

If you visit during Revathi Pattathanam you can attend public lectures, debates and ceremonies associated with the assembly — these are cultural events rather than tourist spectacles, so observe respectfully and confirm schedules in advance.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Tali Temple stands in central Kozhikode (Palayam), about a short distance east of Kozhikode railway station. The area is busy; plan for a short walk from nearby transport hubs and leave time to respect temple dress and conduct rules.

Confirm event dates and visiting rules before you travel. For festivals and scholarly events (Revathi Pattathanam) check official or tourism pages and the temple office; do not rely on fixed daily timings published informally.

visitorInfo.bestTime: Thulam (mid‑October to mid‑November) for Revathi Pattathanam; otherwise October–February for pleasant weather.
visitorInfo.howToReach: In central Kozhikode (Palayam). A short taxi/auto ride from Kozhikode railway station; Kozhikode (Calicut) International Airport is the nearest airport. Confirm local directions on arrival.
etiquette: Dress modestly and follow temple dress codes; carry a mundu/veshti if you plan to enter inner shrines.
Revathi Pattathanam is a scholarly event — be quiet and respectful; photography and entry rules can vary on ceremony days.
Confirm festival dates and visiting hours with official sources or the temple office before travelling.
